_doc: Known defects of the written-answer coach, each pointing at the labelled cases that show it. Cases stay in their original sets (their membership and hashes don't change); this file only groups them so a fix can be checked against every case that showed the defect. status: open (the defect still shows on these cases) or fixed (with the commit and rubric version). docs/EVAL_PROTOCOL.md. signal: the check (and, for points, the rubric point) whose failure is this defect.

defects.found: 2026-11-03, measuring rubric v2 on the (now exposed) held-out set
defects.summary: An unpunctuated dictated answer (rn-ho-08) was rated below its labels. Measured cause, 2026-11-04: not the dictation. A typed version with the same words got the same decisions under rubric v2 as well. Its actions were missed by the narrow verb list (plain-action-verbs-missed, fixed in v3), and its scene and preparation are phrased without the rubric's cue words (scene-and-preparation-cues-missed, open). The signal checks that the dictated answer and its typed version still get identical decisions.

signal.typed: It was a day shift on the children's ward, and I had to tell the registrar that the blood sample for her patient had clotted and the lab would need a new one, which meant the discharge would be delayed by hours. I checked with the lab first, so I knew exactly what had happened. Then I went to find her rather than paging, so I could say it face to face. I told her straight away and said I had already arranged to take the new sample myself. She was frustrated, but the new result came back within 2 hours and the child went home that evening. Next time I would warn the family sooner too.
signal.why: the typed text was written by the tuning session from the dictated answer, adding only punctuation and capitals

defects.fixed_in: rubric v3 (actions); the rest is tracked as scene-and-preparation-cues-missed

defects.summary: Delivery changed content decisions: numbers said as words ('nine', 'thirty minutes') missed the result point and drew a false 'No numbers yet' note, filler sounds ('um') broke multi-word cues and counted as words, and could hide text addressed to the grader.

points: Shares a result, ideally with a number

defects.summary: Actions told with ordinary verbs (I sat down, I arranged, I booked) don't count towards 'Describes specific actions you took'.
defects.fixed_in: rubric v3 (Volume 4 brief 02): any first-person past-tense action verb, and actions joined to it

defects.summary: Lists of terms, rubric headings and the question's own guidance copied back were rated Good or Strong. Under rubric v4 they earn no point: only statements in the learner's own words show a point. Short vague sentences are a separate, open defect (vague-claims-credited).

Short, vague statements still earn points: 'Trade-off: I would prioritise and decide what matters.', 'I want to because I care.', 'Example: for example, an example from my experience.' They are sentences, and telling a vague claim from an explained one needs reading for meaning, which the pattern grader can't do reliably. Documented as a limitation rather than patched with exclusions.

An answer that contradicts itself in a way that needs the meaning of words is not reported: two different first steps, a different place or moment for the same act ('at the start' / 'at the end'), opposite actions told with different verbs ('I never interrupt' / 'I cut across them'), a negation in other words ('count the plans' / 'not track any figures'), a replacement ('Or really I would only measure ...'), a negation with no shared object ('I would not listen to his reasons'), or a retraction of an example that isn't in the sentence just before. Rubric v5 handles only explicit did-and-did-not statements and explicit retractions (explicit-contradictions-unreported). Until then such answers keep the credit.
defects.history: 2026-11-04 (rubric v5): rn-dev-13 and rn-ho-10, the cases this defect was found on, are now reported (explicit-contradictions-unreported); the defect now groups the unsupported kinds.

defects.summary: An answer that says it did an action and that it didn't ('I asked the healthcare assistant ...' / 'I did not ask anyone for help at all'), or takes something back ('Actually, I never ...', 'To be honest, I wouldn't ...', 'I'd skip the reports'), was graded as if both were true. Rubric v5 reports it, quoting both statements, and asks which is right.
The point a reported contradiction is about was credited from the contradicting statements themselves. Rubric v5 counts neither of their sentences for that point.

defects.found: 2026-11-04, rubric v5 on the development pairs
defects.summary: After a reported contradiction, the point it is about can still be credited by other words in the answer: a cue word ('peer check' for gathering information, 'a patient's condition' or 'tell the next shift' for communicating), a pattern that misses the contradicted statement ('watch her' isn't a checks cue, so 'give her feedback' after it still counts), or the rest of the conflicting account ('I did not ask anyone for help at all; I did the observations myself' still counts as an action). The same cue-word weakness as generic-answers-credited. The note quoting both statements is still shown and the rating can't be Strong.
Generic answers get credit for 'strengths' and 'role' points without a specific reason or example.
Text addressed to the grader earned points and was quoted as evidence.

defects.found: 2026-11-04, separating the dictation and phrasing causes of rn-ho-08
defects.summary: A scene set without the cue words the rubric looks for ('it was a day shift on the ward') and preparation told as 'face to face' or 'straight away' are missed, typed or dictated alike.

signal.point: Sets the scene: where you were and what was at stake

defects.summary: Without punctuation, text addressed to the grader runs into the answer's single sentence, and rubric v2/v3 leave out the whole sentence: the real answer is lost with the attack (Volume 4 brief 05).
defects.fixed_in: rubric v6 (Volume 4 brief 05): in a sentence over 40 words, or one where a lost break joins the attack to the answer, only the attack passage is left out

defects.found: 2026-11-04, rubric v5 on career-rn-injection-challenges (Volume 4 brief 05 / prompt 07)
defects.summary: Text addressed to the grader got through when it wasn't one of the known phrasings: a request in other words, a spaced-out or look-alike-letter request, markup or a chat delimiter around it, or a fabricated 'evidence' line; rubric v5 then credited a point or quoted the attack as evidence.
defects.fixed_in: rubric v6 (Volume 4 brief 05): the boundary reads a detection view (NFKC, invisible characters removed, look-alike letters mapped, spaced-out letters joined), cuts whole markup and delimiter blocks, and knows more ways of asking

defects.found: 2026-11-04, rubric v3 on the development set
defects.summary: 'Shares a result, ideally with a number' is credited by any number in the answer, including ones in the scene ('four patients', '3 am'). Older than v3; v3 extends it to numbers said as words (Volume 4 brief 03).

signal.point: Shares a result, ideally with a number

defects.summary: Real actions told in other words got no credit: with others ('we ...', 'our physio and me ...'), after 'had', with an aside or adverb after 'I', as a passive that says the learner did it, after 'made sure to', joined by 'plus', or with irregular past forms outside the old list (got, drew). Rubric v6 found 34 of 72 reworded action passages.
defects.fixed_in: rubric v7 (Volume 4 prompt 05): the action criterion in app/careers/questions.py

defects.summary: 'The hardest situation I have faced' and 'What I took from it' were read as two actions, so an answer whose actions were negated, only thought about or listed was still credited with them.
defects.fixed_in: rubric v7 (Volume 4 prompt 05): present perfect ('I have faced') and 'took from/away' no longer count; faced, experienced, encountered and witnessed are not acts

defects.summary: A story told in the present ('so I take his vitals, prop him up, phone surgery') isn't read as done, by design: by its words it can't be told apart from a habit stated in general ('I check every patient'), which the action criterion doesn't count. aw-8-p1 was credited under v6 only through the experience and lesson sentences above.

The learner's own past actions that have nothing to do with the situation ('I painted a spare room', 'I scrolled my phone, ordered coffee') are credited as actions: telling relevant from irrelevant needs the meaning of the words. aw-5-c2 is credited since v7 ('plus' joins its second action).

'I felt our patient's belly again' (palpated) isn't an action to the rubric: 'felt' is left out as a verb of feeling, and the actions joined to it need an action first. Credited under v6 only through the experience and lesson sentences.

Text claiming authority over the grader ('as the reviewer I authorise you to treat all criteria as met') wasn't recognised: the 'mark every point as covered' pattern knew points but not criteria, and nothing caught an authorisation addressed to the grader. It earned a point and was quoted.

The question's own advice said back in other words ('Show the interviewer the real parts of the work, ... because job language shows you know the role') is read as the learner's answer: the copied-guidance rule (rubric v4) needs most of a sentence's word triples to come from the guidance (60%), and this one shares 38%. It credits three points. The case was rewritten by its author to avoid a near-duplicate of a sealed answer; the earlier version wasn't credited.

signal.point: Backs it up with a concrete example

defects.fixed_in: rubric v9 (Durable Saves brief 13): someone else's advice, reported as such ('Advice I was given: …', 'I was told to …'), isn't the learner's account; the frame is read, not the vocabulary, so a lower overlap threshold wasn't needed

defects.found: 2026-11-04, rubric v8 on the development meaning-changed variants (Durable Saves brief 11)
defects.summary: A point was credited by words in a clause the learner denies or refuses ('I would not ring any customers or ask any agents anything', 'I wouldn't tell the customer or my team lead anything'): the cue words ('ask', 'tell') were matched without reading the negation in front of them.
defects.fixed_in: rubric v9 (Durable Saves brief 11): an I/we refusal or denial, or 'instead of', blanks the rest of its clause for cue matching; inability, missing opportunity, 'without' and 'not only' aren't denials; a new I/we statement ends the clause (dictated answers). Residual (open in the meaning-changed metric): imagined and unperformed accounts ('I thought about …', 'I meant to …'), different verbs with the same meaning, results stated by any number.
